title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall
summary: Budget forecasts show growth in living standards grinding almost to a halt.
paragraphs: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall
People are facing a "painful" and "depressing" few years ahead, economic think tanks have warned, after forecasts showed growth in living standards grinding almost to a halt.

Typical working-age households would see their disposable income fall by £1,050, or 3%, between now and 2029, according to the Resolution Foundation, while the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) said the current decade would be the worst for household income growth on record.
Chancellor John Healey said his Budget offered "breathing space", but said the government could "never remove completely" cost of living pressures.
The UK's official forecaster said its latest economic forecast painted a "pretty grim picture".
The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), blamed the difficult financial situation facing the UK on higher borrowing costs and inflation caused by the US-Iran war.
In response to rising energy prices, Healey has announced measures, including a £100 support payment, aimed at easing pressure on household finances.
But that would not be enough to offset the impact of higher energy bills, the Resolution Foundation said.
"This parliament is increasingly looking like one of two halves," said the think tank's chief executive, Ruth Curtice.
"The first half has been marked by rising living standards, solid economic growth and extra funding for public services," she said.
However, the second half of the parliament would be "tough going", she said.
- Treasury will not commit to reducing welfare bill before next election
- What we now know about the UK economy in four charts
- Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you
In response to this "painful" situation the government had provided a "scattergun" Budget that did not do enough to address the challenges facing the country, Curtice said.

Over the course of this parliament, incomes for non-pensioner households, after taxes, benefits, and housing costs are taken into account, will have risen by "a paltry" £600, the Resolution Foundation said, with the gains "already behind us".
Even after the extra support provided by the government, households will be left paying higher energy bills than during the last energy crisis in 2022, according to its analysis.
The Resolution Foundation said the support should have been more targeted at the poorest households.
Alongside the Budget the OBR issued its economic forecast indicating a slowdown in GDP growth from 1.2% in 2026 to 1% in 2027.
The forecast for next year is sharply lower than what was predicted at their last assessment in March.
The OBR also put its forecast for inflation for 2027 up from 2% to 3.4%.
Frozen tax thresholds are also eating into people's take-home pay.

However, the OBR also emphasised the difficulties in economic forecasting, highlighting uncertainty over the future path of inflation, in particular, which could turn out to be either significantly higher or lower than their predictions.

While the Resolution Foundation focused its forecast for living standards on working age households, the OBR looks at all households, including pensioners and reflects a 10-year rolling average growth to take into account short-term fluctuations.
The OBR found that by the end of the decade living standards for all households would have barely grown, by less than 0.1% per year.
Helen Miller, director of the influential think tank, the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) said the outlook was "depressing".
"This decade looks set to be the worst decade for growth in household incomes on record," she said.
"No amount of temporary cost of living packages will fix that. We need a stronger economy."
There would also be growing pressure on the government's spending plans over the parliament, Miller added.
"Spending plans look extremely tight. They don't look to me like plans that this government would want to deliver," she said.
"Whether or not they are delivered matters because the spending plans underpin the plan to bring down borrowing," she added.
Miller said she was left with the impression that Healey was hoping the economy would improve to take the pressure off those spending decisions.

Healey, speaking on the BBC's Today Programme, said "economic storms", including the Iran war and Russia's invasion of Ukraine, were affecting countries around the world and the government was seeking to help where it could.
He said energy bill help would create "breathing space" for most households.
Around 20 million households are set to receive the £100 payment based on which council tax band they are in.

But Conservative shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith said the Budget had left the public finances "more fragile" as Healey had reduced the "headroom" or the buffer that the country has between what it takes in revenues and what it spends.

Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey said the £100 energy payment would be identified as the best item in the Budget for many people, but said that it was "not good enough" when you considered the "stealth tax rises" that were taking money out of people's pay packets.

paragraphs: Νεκρός 23χρονος που «χτυπήθηκε» από ηλεκτρικό ρεύμα στο Αγρίνιο
Τραγωδία σημειώθηκε το απόγευμα της Πέμπτης (29/10) στο Αγρίνιο όταν ένας 23χρονος «χτυπήθηκε» από ηλεκτρικό ρεύμα.
Το τραγικό περιστατικό σύμφωνα με το Agriniopress έγινε στην περιοχή Καλύβια όταν ο νεαρός Ρομά ήρθε σε επαφή με το ηλεκτρικό ρεύμα την ώρα που έκανε εργασίες σε αποθήκη.

Οι περίοικοι ειδοποίησαν αμέσως το ΕΚΑΒ ωστόσο μόλις αντιλήφθηκαν την κατάστασή του, αποφάσισαν να μην περιμένουν την άφιξη του ασθενοφόρου και τον μετέφεραν οι ίδιοι στο νοσοκομείο. Εκει οι γιατροί έδωσαν μάχη για να τον κρατήσουν στη ζωή.
Δυστυχώς όμως, λίγο αργότερα επιβεβαιώθηκε ο θάνατός του.

title: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm
summary: It will cause huge disruption in some parts of England and Wales, say GP leaders.
paragraphs: Hundreds of GP practices lose online services after collapse of tech firm
Patients in many parts of the country have been left unable to access their GP surgery online after a tech firm went into administration.
Silicon Practice ran digital services, including websites, online booking and consultations, for around 500 practices in England – just under 10% of the total.
Practices across the country, including in London, Gloucestershire and Norfolk, have reported problems. Services in Wales are also affected.
GP leaders said the problem would cause huge disruption, given the scale of online booking that now takes places.
Patients in areas that are affected are being advised they will have to make appointments via the phone. The NHS app is working.
Since last year, all practices in England have had to offer online appointment booking. Currently, more than 40% of appointments are made that way.
An NHS England spokesperson said while "the majority" of GP practice websites were running as normal, some using Silicon Practice will be affected.
"If your GP practice website is unavailable and you need help, you should contact your practice by phone or in person as usual."
Affected practices have been contacted by NHS England with advice on how to maintain business continuity and minimise the impact on patient care.

Silicon Practice ran the digital tool FootFall, which it advertised as reducing patient phone calls to practices by 30%, by working to "free your reception team from routine admin and manage demand more efficiently. Proven in 1,000+ GP practices across the UK".

Prof Victoria Tzortziou Brown, president of the Royal College of GPs, said: "GP practice websites are an increasingly important way for patients to access care, book appointments and find information about the services available to them.
"When websites are not working, it can be hugely disruptive for patients and place additional pressures on already stretched practice teams.
"It is vital that any disruption to practice websites is addressed promptly to ensure patients are able to access care."

She said affected practices must receive prompt, practical support from NHS England and local NHS organisations to restore their websites, minimise disruption and ensure patients know how to contact their practice and access the care they need in the meantime.

title: Αυξήθηκε στους 74 ο αριθμός των νεκρών του τραγικού δυστυχήματος στην Ισπανία
summary: Σε τουλάχιστον 74 ανέρχεται ο αριθμός των νεκρών στη χθεσινή σύγκρουση δύο τρένων στην Ισπανία, σύμφωνα με νέο απολογισμό που έδωσε στη δημοσιότητα σήμερα η Επιτροπή Διερεύνησης Σιδηροδρομικών Δυστυχημάτων του...Περισσότερα...
paragraphs: Αυξήθηκε στους 74 ο αριθμός των νεκρών του τραγικού δυστυχήματος στην Ισπανία

Σε τουλάχιστον 74 ανέρχεται ο αριθμός των νεκρών στη χθεσινή σύγκρουση δύο τρένων στην Ισπανία, σύμφωνα με νέο απολογισμό που έδωσε στη δημοσιότητα σήμερα η Επιτροπή Διερεύνησης Σιδηροδρομικών Δυστυχημάτων του υπουργείου Μεταφορών.
Προηγούμενος απολογισμός από τις αρχές της περιφέρειας Καστίλλη-Λα Μάντσα, όπου συνέβη το δυστύχημα, ανέφερε 69 θανάτους.

Μετά την επίσκεψή του σε νοσοκομείο στο Τολέδο όπου νοσηλεύονται τραυματίες του σιδηροδρομικού δυστυχημάτος, ο βασιλιάς Φελίπε ΣΤ΄ ζήτησε σήμερα τη λήψη «μέτρων» για την αποτροπή μιας ακόμη σιδηροδρομικής καταστροφής.
«Η έρευνα πρέπει να προσδιορίσει πώς και γιατί συνέβη αυτή η καταστροφή. Πρέπει επίσης να μελετήσουμε τα μέτρα που πρέπει να ληφθούν για να διασφαλίσουμε ότι αυτό δεν θα ξανασυμβεί ποτέ», δήλωσε.

title: Καππαδοκία: Τρεις οι νεκροί από την κατάρρευση καμινάδας της Νεράϊδας - Ξεκίνησε έρευνα
summary: Τρεις άνθρωποι έχασαν τη ζωή τους και πέντε τραυματίστηκαν από κατολίσθηση ενός βραχώδους σχηματισμού σε τουριστικό χώρο στην ιστορική περιοχή της Καππαδοκίας, στην Τουρκία και σύμφωνα με τις τελευταίες πληροφορίες, για...Περισσότερα...
paragraphs: Καππαδοκία: Τρεις οι νεκροί από την κατάρρευση καμινάδας της Νεράϊδας - Ξεκίνησε έρευνα

Τρεις άνθρωποι έχασαν τη ζωή τους και πέντε τραυματίστηκαν από κατολίσθηση ενός βραχώδους σχηματισμού σε τουριστικό χώρο στην ιστορική περιοχή της Καππαδοκίας, στην Τουρκία και σύμφωνα με τις τελευταίες πληροφορίες, για το περιστατικό έχει ξεκινήσει έρευνα.

Σύμφωνα με το τουρκικό πρακτορείο Anadolu, η ισχυρή βροχόπτωση προκάλεσε την αποκόλληση βράχων από έναν από τους χαρακτηριστικούς γεωλογικούς σχηματισμούς της περιοχής, γνωστούς ως «νεραϊδοκαμινάδες», κοντά στο Υπαίθριο Μουσείο του Γκιόρεμε.

Τα βράχια κατέπεσαν σε σημείο όπου βρίσκονταν επισκέπτες και άλλοι πολίτες. Στην περιοχή έσπευσαν αστυνομικές δυνάμεις, χωροφυλακή, διασώστες της τουρκικής υπηρεσίας αντιμετώπισης καταστροφών AFAD και ασθενοφόρα.

Αρχικά εντοπίστηκαν δύο νεκροί κάτω από τα συντρίμμια, ενώ στη συνέχεια οι διασώστες ανέσυραν τη σορό ενός ακόμη ανθρώπου, ανεβάζοντας τον απολογισμό στους τρεις νεκρούς. Πέντε τραυματίες μεταφέρθηκαν σε νοσοκομείο της Νεβσεχίρ.

Ο κυβερνήτης της επαρχίας Νεβσεχίρ, Χουσεΐν Κοκ, δήλωσε ότι οι σοροί των θυμάτων ανασύρθηκαν από τα συντρίμμια, ωστόσο ο υπουργός Δικαιοσύνης προειδοποίησε ότι ενδέχεται να υπάρχουν και άλλα θύματα που παραμένουν εγκλωβισμένα.
Η κατάρρευση ενδέχεται να προκλήθηκε από την έντονη βροχόπτωση

Ο νομάρχης της επαρχίας Νεβσεχίρ, Χουσεΐν Κιοκ, ο οποίος μετέβη στο σημείο της καταστροφής, απέδωσε την κατολίσθηση στις έντονες βροχοπτώσεις και ανακοίνωσε την κινητοποίηση όλων των διαθέσιμων κρατικών μέσων για την αντιμετώπιση του περιστατικού.
Σύμφωνα με τουρκικά μέσα ενημέρωσης, η κατάρρευση σημειώθηκε κοντά στην είσοδο του μουσείου, περίπου στις 15:15 τοπική ώρα (12:15 GMT).

Παράλληλα με τις επιχειρήσεις διάσωσης, οι τουρκικές δικαστικές αρχές διέταξαν έρευνα για τις συνθήκες υπό τις οποίες σημειώθηκε η κατολίσθηση. Ο υπουργός Δικαιοσύνης της Τουρκίας, Ακίν Γκιουρλέκ, ανακοίνωσε ότι η Εισαγγελία του Νεβσεχίρ ανέλαβε τη διερεύνηση του περιστατικού, ορίζοντας τρεις εισαγγελικούς λειτουργούς.
Οι επιχειρήσεις των σωστικών συνεργείων στην περιοχή συνεχίζονται, σύμφωνα με το πρακτορείο Ανατολή.

«Μετά την κατάρρευση μιας "νεραϊδοκαμινάδας" στην κωμόπολη Γκιόρεμε, στην επαρχία Νεβσεχίρ, η Εισαγγελία του Νεβσεχίρ ξεκίνησε άμεσα έρευνα, αναθέτοντας την υπόθεση σε έναν αναπληρωτή προϊστάμενο εισαγγελέα και δύο εισαγγελείς», ανέφερε ο Γκιουρλέκ.

Σημειώνεται πως η περιοχή της Καππαδοκίας προσελκύει τουρίστες από όλο τον κόσμο, οι οποίοι έρχονται για να δουν τις περίφημες «νεραϊδοκαμινάδες» - ψηλούς, κωνικούς βραχώδεις σχηματισμούς που δημιουργήθηκαν από ηφαιστειακή δραστηριότητα.

title: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
summary: With 99% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its allies are set to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.
paragraphs: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show

Partial results from Israel's general election show veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu marginally ahead of his rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, but still short of a majority in parliament.

With 99% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies were on track to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. Eisenkot's Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc were set for 48.
Both leaders have said they will try to form a governing coalition.
Arab-led parties, which are on course to win an unprecedented 19 seats, could emerge as kingmakers. But all but one of the Jewish parties have pledged not to work with them.
On Thursday, officials began counting as many as 480,000 absentee ballots from groups including soldiers, diplomats and hospital patients, who could not get to polling stations.
These votes may change the final number of seats allotted to each party under Israel's proportional representation system.

Once the results are confirmed, President Isaac Herzog will hold consultations with all the political factions and invite the leader whom he believes has the best chance of success to form a government - a process that could take weeks.
If they fail, then ultimately there would have to be another election.
- Israel's election deadlock is a sign of the country's deep divisions
- How could Israel break election deadlock? Here are four scenarios
During a meeting at his residence in Jerusalem on Wednesday, Herzog praised the 77.7% turnout in the previous day's election, which was the highest in more than two decades.
"It is a badge of honour for Israeli society, and it was remarkable to see how deep the desire for democracy is in Israel," he said.
He added that he expected to receive the official results next week, after which he would begin discussions with every faction.
"We must do everything we can, certainly after yesterday, to avoid another round of elections. So, I expect everyone who comes here to come with an open mind."
Both the prime minister and his main rival have insisted that they should be tasked with forming a governing coalition.

Eisenkot declared that the public had "spoken in favour of change", after initial exit polls published by three Israeli broadcasters projected that his "Change Bloc" would emerge with between 52 and 53 seats in the Knesset, compared to 50 seats for Netanyahu's bloc.

"The coalition of failure has lost the people's trust," he told supporters at Yashar's election headquarters in Tel Aviv. "I will work with my partners to ensure that the people's decision is translated into a Zionist government."
Later, the broadcasters updated their exit polls, with two projecting that the rival blocs would be tied on 51 seats and one giving Netanyahu's bloc a narrow three-seat lead.
Netanyahu then appeared at Likud's headquarters in Jerusalem and declared that his right-wing bloc had won a "great majority".
"We must put in place a strong right-wing national government," he said. "It is forbidden, simply forbidden, to endanger Israel by forming a government that relies on anti-Zionist Arab parties."

As the votes were counted, it emerged that his bloc had done better than the exit polls predicted and was on course to win 53 seats. However, that figure is 15 seats fewer than it had once controlled in the last Knesset.
Tuesday's election was the first since the deadly Hamas-led attacks on Israel on 7 October 2023 and the wars that followed in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.

It was also seen by Israelis as one of the most consequential in the country's history, because it could decide not just their leadership but whether the country continues on its current hard-line, religious-nationalist trajectory.

Key campaign issues included accountability for the security failures that led to the 7 October attacks, the conduct of regional wars, conscripting ultra-Orthodox Jewish men into the military, judicial reforms and Israel's international standing.
Avigail Levine from Kfar Saba, who voted for former prime minister Naftali Bennett's opposition Beyachad party, told the BBC that she was disappointed with the election results.
"I was hoping for new leadership. I feel we need it as a nation," she said. "The people in power on 7 October should not be in power now."

She said people were frustrated that Netanyahu had not shouldered responsibility for what happened three years ago, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage. Her husband's grandmother was among those who died in Kibbutz Be'eri.
Gal from Ramat Gan said he voted for Netanyahu because Israelis "cannot relax and live in peace with neighbours when all they want is to erase us from the map".
He also said he was "afraid of the strengthening of the Arab political parties".

The two Arab parties - the United Arab List and the Joint List - are set to almost double their representation because of a surge in turnout among Arab Israelis, who account for about a fifth of the population and often describe themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel.
Mahdi Kabaha, who lives in a village near Haifa and campaigned to get out the Arab vote, described the result as "historic".
"Arab citizens came out and said clearly: we want a real say in this country," he said.

The head of the Joint List, Yousef Jabareen, told the BBC that Arab voters had been motivated in part by the opportunity to remove far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir from office, whom he accused of racism and "provocation against our community".

Ben-Gvir, the leader of the Jewish Power party, has called for the annexation of the occupied West Bank, Jewish settlement of Gaza, and the "voluntary emigration" of Palestinians. Several Western countries have imposed sanctions on him for incitement against Palestinians.

United Arab List leader Mansour Abbas, who served in a short-lived governing coalition formed after the 2021 elections, said on Tuesday night that he hoped "the numbers will work out and we, the Change Bloc and the UAL, can ensure that there are 61 Knesset seats".

The leader of the left-wing Democrats party, Yair Golan, told his partners in Eisenkot's bloc that there was an "opportunity to form a change government in partnership" with the Arab parties and replace Netanyahu's coalition.
"We have no future here if we don't stop being afraid. And if we don't put an end to racism," he wrote on X.

Eisenkot has previously raised objections or attached conditions to that kind of alliance, including recognising Israel as Jewish and democratic, and Hamas as a terrorist organisation that must be destroyed. The right-wing parties in his bloc, meanwhile, have flatly rejected it.

"The opposition parties cannot dictate any conditions," Jabareen said. "If the opposition in Israel are willing to afford real and substantive change, and an alternative for the dangerous, extreme-right-wing government... they will have to negotiate with us."
Netanyahu's Likud party has accused the Arab parties of "stealing" the election.

It complained to the Central Elections Committee (CEC) on Wednesday that they had resorted to "bribery, threats, violence, fraud and the use of prohibited software to encourage voters", without providing any evidence. The CEC said it would examine the allegations as part of a comprehensive post-election review.

On Thursday, CEC chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg instructed the Shin Bet domestic security service to investigate what he described as "serious suspicions" regarding "improper influence through foreign funding by external actors operating against Israeli interests".

He gave no further details, but the Haaretz newspaper cited a source as saying the committee had been presented with a claim that the Gulf state of Qatar had provided funding aimed at increasing voter turnout in Arab communities.
"This is an attack on democracy aimed at enabling foreign control of the Knesset, the Islamization of Israel, and the removal of the right-wing government," Likud said.

But Balad chairman Sami Abu Shehadeh, who is part of the Joint List, dismissed the allegation, saying: "The losing side is constructing a racist blood libel and calling on the security agencies to use force in order to overturn the election results."

Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman, Majed al-Ansari, denied that it had interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome. "The accusations are ridiculous and dangerous in equal measure," he warned.

title: Offshore workers turn to weight-loss jabs to meet helicopter weight rules
summary: From Sunday anyone weighing more than 19st 7Ib (124kg) will be banned from flying to an offshore platform.
paragraphs: Offshore workers turn to weight-loss jabs to meet helicopter weight rules
Hundreds of offshore workers have been using weight-loss jabs to help meet maximum weight rules for helicopter flights due to come into force next week.
From Sunday, anyone weighing more than 19st 7Ib (124kg) in civilian clothing and footwear will be banned from taking a flight to an offshore platform covered by UK safety regulations.
When the new rules were announced last year, about 2,200 workers were over the limit but that figure has now fallen to fewer than 250, according to Offshore Energies UK (OEUK).
The industry body told BBC Scotland News that on one platform, 60% of staff had been taking weight-loss drugs and extra fridge space had been provided to keep the medications cool.
The average weight of offshore workers has risen over recent decades, and increased by almost 1st 7Ib (10kg) since 2008.
The new weight limit policy came after the Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA) warned that rescue winches - which are critical during offshore emergencies - cannot safely lift heavier people.
The figure was decided upon after factoring in the weight of the rescuer, stretcher and other kit that would add to the combined total.
OEUK health and safety manager Graham Skinner said a range of measures were being used to help offshore workers manage their weight, including gym equipment and healthier food options.
Alongside those, he said many had had chosen to make use of the latest medical advances in controlling appetite and digestion.

"What we know is that offshore workers are using weight-loss jabs regardless of the policies. Last year we saw in some cases 60% of workers turning up with weight-loss jabs," he told BBC Scotland News.

"That's brought our average weight down in a very short space of time. I think that's very common in society and it can potentially be a really useful tool if somebody's got a lot of weight to lose it can get them in a good place."
He said initially staff appeared to be funding the medication themselves, although he thought it possible that some firms were now supporting them with the costs.

The weight-limit policy has been criticised by the RMT union, external which claimed there had been a lack of consultation, and that it could lead to experienced staff being excluded from offshore operations.
Earlier this year, BBC Scotland spoke to one occupational health expert in Aberdeen who said some clients were "really stressed" by the new rules while others had chosen to leave the industry.
Companies could offer staff alternative onshore roles but Skinner warned: "If somebody has chosen not to lose weight then there's a real possibility they could lose their job."

He said there were a number of safety reasons for having weight-limit controls such as working in confined spaces or ability to quickly exit a helicopter - but the actual numbers had been driven by the lifting capacity of the winches.

"It's the same winch on all search and rescue helicopters and if somebody needs to be rescued due to a health or safety incident the winch has limitations and we can't allow people to exceed those," he said.
Workers will be asked to declare if they are under the weight limit and this will be checked at the heliport.

He said employers in the industry had been working "really hard" to ensure as many staff as possible complied with the new rules and he hoped the number of staff over the weight limit could be reduced still further.

title: 'The city is alive': A brief peace in Kherson, but residents fear what comes next
summary: A temporary ceasefire has brought rare quiet to Kherson, offering its residents a glimpse of normal life before fighting resumes.
paragraphs: 'The city is alive': A brief peace in Kherson, but residents fear what comes next

The Ukrainian city of Kherson has known its first two days of quiet after many years, as a US-brokered temporary ceasefire has allowed residents rare moments of respite from the constant Russian aerial attacks that plague the front line region.

Videos posted on social media showed people strolling down streets covered in anti-drone nets and gathering in the city's squares - ordinary activities that usually mean keeping one eye on the sky and one ear out for incoming drones.
"Ever since the ceasefire was announced, there's been total silence," said Olga, 42, speaking by phone from Kherson. "We are all, of course, overjoyed."
"I don't even know what to call it," she added, her smile coming through in her voice. "It's as if everything has finally come to an end."
Since Tuesday, Kherson has "literally come back to life," Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said.
"People are calmly going out, walking, enjoying the autumn sun. What for some is ordinary everyday life, for residents of the Kherson region today is the greatest desire."

The temporary pause in hostilities - due to end on Sunday - is the result of efforts by US First Lady Melania Trump to broker a safe passage out of the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, which lies on the other side of the Dnipro river from Kherson.
For several days, Russian forces have been working to clear the road of mines, ahead of a planned evacuation of Oleshky's civilians on Friday.

But there are fears that, alongside carrying out the well-publicised "humanitarian operation" – which some American journalists will be invited to witness – the Russians are using the truce to bolster their forces in the area ahead of a renewed onslaught of Kherson from next week.

"They are... using this lull to strengthen their positions, bring in more military supplies, weapons, ammunition, and drones, and carry out some redeployment of their forces," an anonymous source working in local government told the BBC.

Petro Andriushchenko, Director of Ukraine's Center for Studying the Occupation, says Kherson locals have told him that they witnessed a military build-up around Radensk, some 20km (12 miles) from Oleshky.

Its residents will be saved but "we are simultaneously giving the enemy an opportunity to exploit the ceasefire for its own military purposes," he said. Once the ceasefire ends, the situation may be "worse than we saw before, because Russia's units will be stronger. They have enough time to prepare to prolong this action."
Though Kherson residents are clear-eyed about what lies ahead, for a brief period this week the city caught its breath.
No violations have been reported on either side since Tuesday. There have been other ceasefires in the past, but these were generally not respected, Kherson resident Dima said.
"This is the first time the shelling has stopped, people don't quite believe it," he told the BBC. "They are going to the shops, drinking coffee, walking around... The city is alive."

On social media, a woman named Yulia wrote about her unusually uneventful trip to the supermarket with an edge of disbelief. For once, she said, she returned home from the shops "whole and calm, not as usual - scared, sweating from the horror and with a lump in my throat."

This week, dozens of people were also able to access their belongings and homes in the so-called "red zone" of Kherson – an area so exposed to drones and artillery attacks that it has become unlivable.

"Some are venturing into places where nobody has dared to go for years, filming areas where simply being present has meant - and will once again mean - almost certain death," said Denisa Bohackova, a Czech volunteer who lives in Kherson.
Dima described scenes of "girls, boys, parents, grandmothers" walking down the streets of the red zone carrying suitcases and bags, returning to their flats to see what they could retrieve.

Some of those who returned to the red zone found buildings reduced to charred, empty shells; in other cases, homes had been looted. The scale of destruction in some of these places, Bohackova said, is "breathtaking".

Others were rushing back for reasons beyond material concerns. Angela Dobrovolska's husband Serhiy was killed two years ago by a grenade dropped by a piloted Russian drone - an instance of a "human safari" attack of the kind that Kherson has become sadly infamous for.

On Thursday, Angela headed back from Kyiv to Kherson to visit his grave for the first time in months. "They say that all the people have rushed to Kherson," she said. "And I'll be going to the cemetery to my husband."
The population of Kherson has dwindled from over 250,000 to about 65,000 since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, which will enter its sixth year in February.

Though civilian life in the city never stopped, Bohackova said, it also carried on under the conditions of an active battlefield, with schools, theatres, kindergartens and hospitals moved underground.
"An ordinary civilian from Kherson has experienced more of this war than many soldiers," Bohackova said.
Olga, who is raising two children, described regular blackouts, mines dropped by drones and concealed by fallen leaves, drone fragments ricocheting, and a city that typically shuts by the afternoon.

But since silence fell on the city, Olga has been able to live a normal life. She drove to a different town and took the bus to another district to visit her grandmother with her son. Around her, the shops were full, as were the cafes. After years of quiet streets, "there was even a small traffic jam," she smiled.
The evacuation of nearby Oleshky is due to be completed by Sunday, after which the ceasefire will be over. "The concern is that, starting Monday, things could turn truly chaotic," Olga said.
"We know the strikes will resume, and that they will increase," said Dima, as he and his wife prepared to visit their flat in the red zone for the first time in several months.
"These few days showed us how it could be if it all finally ended."
body:
The Ukrainian city of Kherson has known its first two days of quiet after many years, as a US-brokered temporary ceasefire has allowed residents rare moments of respite from the constant Russian aerial attacks that plague the front line region.

Videos posted on social media showed people strolling down streets covered in anti-drone nets and gathering in the city's squares - ordinary activities that usually mean keeping one eye on the sky and one ear out for incoming drones.

"Ever since the ceasefire was announced, there's been total silence," said Olga, 42, speaking by phone from Kherson. "We are all, of course, overjoyed."

"I don't even know what to call it," she added, her smile coming through in her voice. "It's as if everything has finally come to an end."

Since Tuesday, Kherson has "literally come back to life," Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said.

"People are calmly going out, walking, enjoying the autumn sun. What for some is ordinary everyday life, for residents of the Kherson region today is the greatest desire."

The temporary pause in hostilities - due to end on Sunday - is the result of efforts by US First Lady Melania Trump to broker a safe passage out of the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, which lies on the other side of the Dnipro river from Kherson.

title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
summary: Former President Donald Trump has been indicted by a Manhattan grand jury, marking the first time in US history that a current or former president has faced criminal charges.
paragraphs: Our live coverage of Trump’s historic indictment has moved.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan wrote his Monday night order that the media’s request to broadcast the arraignment of former President Donald Trump was understandable, but that the news organizations’ interests in providing the broadest possible access to the proceedings must be weighed against “competing interests.”
In rejecting the request to broadcast the arraignment live on television, Merchan still wrote about the historical significance of the proceeding in stark terms.

“That this indictment involves a matter of monumental significance cannot possibly be disputed. Never in the history of the United States has a sitting or past President been indicted on criminal charges. Mr. Trump’s arraignment has generated unparalleled public interest and media attention,” he wrote. “The populace rightly hungers for the most accurate and current information available. To suggest otherwise would be disingenuous.”

News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.
However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”
Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.
The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.
Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

Donald Trump is not planning to speak publicly in New York on Tuesday, aides say, if he follows advice from members of his legal team who have urged the former President to refrain from the vitriol he’s been directing toward the prosecutor and judge presiding over the case.

But that restraint does not extend to Florida, aides said, where he is planning to deliver a full-throated defense of his New York case as well as other investigations he is facing during a prime time address from Mar-a-Lago on Tuesday night.
It’s the first test to see whether Trump can navigate two vasty different approaches to his legal case and his political campaign, which are now inextricably linked.
“He’s taking this very seriously and following legal advice,” an adviser to Trump said Monday night. “He will make his case to Americans Tuesday night at Mar-a-Lago.”

Alina Habba, who represents Donald Trump in several civil matters, spent time with the former president in New York today and said, “He’s in good spirits. Honestly, he’s as he normally would be. He’s ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow.”
Habba — appearing on on Fox News’ “Jesse Watters” — was asked about the “game plan” for Trump’s appearance in court in Manhattan Tuesday and said, “It’s all mapped out.”
She added, “Barring any surprises, I think that it should be smooth. We’re trying to coordinate and cooperate with everybody to make sure that there are no problems.”

On whether Trump can get a fair trial in Manhattan, Habba said, “No, no. I think it’s very difficult. I’d like to have faith in this state, but I’ve been practicing for him now for a couple years and gone to court in New York for a few years, and I can tell you, it’s not the same as representing anybody else.”
Former President Donald Trump met with his attorneys Susan Necheles and Joe Tacopina at Trump Tower after arriving in New York City Monday, a source familiar with the meeting told CNN.
It is unclear if the newest addition to Trump’s New York legal team, Todd Blanche, attended the meeting.
Former President Donald Trump has landed in New York’s La Guardia Airport ahead of his expected Tuesday arraignment in a Manhattan courthouse.
History was made Thursday when he was indicted by a New York grand jury. It’s the first time that a current or former US president has been criminally charged.

The Manhattan district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme and cover-up involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential campaign.
Trump’s attorney said he plans to file “substantial” legal challenges. The former president has repeatedly denied wrongdoing in the matter and accused Democrats of targeting him politically.
See more photos of the days leading up to Trump’s indictment:

A small group of supporters chanted as former President Donald Trump arrived at his namesake tower on Monday afternoon, with a handful of people waving banners with messages like “Trump won” and “Arrest Biden.”
While Trump couldn’t see his admirers as he entered a side door on 56th Street, his arrival came with more fanfare and security than at any other time in his post presidency.

Now that he is inside the building — where he launched his presidential bid nearly eight years ago — Trump is expected to meet with lawyers and political advisers on the eve of his arraignment, an aide told CNN.
Trump’s mood was described by an adviser as “defiant and focused,” as he watched expansive television coverage while flying back to his native New York City from Florida.

Special counsel prosecutors have secured evidence including daily notes, texts, emails and photographs and are focused on cataloging how Donald Trump handled classified records around the Mar-a-Lago resort and those who may have witnessed the former president with them, according to multiple sources familiar with the investigation.
The new details come amid signs the Justice Department is taking steps that are typically near the end of an investigation.

The recent investigative activity before a federal grand jury in Washington, DC, also includes subpoenaing witnesses in March and April who had previously spoken to investigators, the sources said. While the FBI interviewed many aides and workers at Mar-a-Lago nearly a year ago voluntarily, grand jury appearances are transcribed and under oath — an indication the prosecutors are locking in witness testimony.

The focus of both the mishandling of records and obstruction of justice probes has remained on the actions of the former president, the sources say. That includes prosecutors pursuing evidence of Trump’s intent to keep classified records after he left the White House, plus his knowledge that the records remained in his possession after the Justice Department demanded their return last May.
Witnesses are being questioned about what they saw in Trump’s private residential and work areas within the club, some of the sources said.
Former President Donald Trump has arrived at his midtown Manhattan property Trump Tower.
He will stay at Trump Tower tonight and is expected to depart New York immediately after Tuesday’s arraignment to head back to Florida — where he plans to deliver remarks at his Mar-a-lago home.
President Joe Biden told CNN’s Betsy Klein he isn’t worried about unrest due to former President Donald Trump’s criminal indictment in New York.
“No, I have faith in the New York Police Department,” Biden said on Monday during a tour of a power generation facility in Fridley, Minnesota.
Asked if he had faith in the legal system, Biden replied: “Yes.”
As former President Donald Trump walked down from his plane at La Guardia Airport on the eve of his arraignment, CNN’s Gloria Borger noted the unique situation he’s in.

Trump is “one of the most famous people in the world, and he is a former president, presidential candidate, and now he’s a defendant. We haven’t seen that. It’s hard to kind of process that,” Borger said to CNN’s Dana Bash.
Borger also highlighted how Trump’s day in court is something he’s avoided for decades and that it will be a grievance he uses to rile up his supporters.

“Donald Trump is somebody who’s probably tried to avoid his day in court for a very long time — decades. And now, you know, you have this man who is saying to people who support him, ‘You know I am your retribution.’ And he is going to make his grievance their grievance. And I think we’re going to see that play out over and over again, and we’ll see it play out in court with his attorney,” she said.
CNN’s Audie Cornish noted how Trump ending up in court seemed unavoidable given the “sheer number of investigations against him.”
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan said he’ll likely issue a decision tonight on whether media outlets can broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday.
CNN is part of the media coalition that asked the judge for permission to broadcast the hearing.
More on this: Trump’s attorneys said in their letter to Merchan that he is required under court rules to take into account potential security concerns.

“As Your Honor is well-aware, this case presents extraordinary security concerns (including Secret Service-related concerns) and we submit that any video or photography of the proceedings will only heighten these serious concerns,” they wrote.
The Manhattan District Attorney’s office also responded Monday to the news outlets’ request and said that it was deferring to the judge to make a decision on how best to manage his courtroom.

Donald Trump — the first former president in history to face criminal charges — has arrived in New York for an expected arraignment on Tuesday after being indicted last week by a Manhattan grand jury.

The former president will stay at Trump Tower tonight, according to a source familiar with his plans. But even before Trump’s appearance, his presence will be felt in the Manhattan courthouse Tuesday, as all trials and most other court activity is being halted before he is slated to arrive.
Here is what we know about tomorrow’s events:

CNN’s John Miller, Jeremy Herb, Katelyn Polantz, Tierney Sneed, Sydney Kashiwagi, Kristen Holmes, Holmes Lybrand, Hannah Rabinowitz, Paula Reid, Alayna Treene, Gregory Clary and Devan Cole contributed reporting to this post.
The former president touched down shortly after 3:25 p.m. ET.

Trump faces more than 30 counts related to business fraud, CNN has reported, but the indictment remains under seal. He is the first current or former president to face criminal charges in American history.
He will spend Monday night at the Trump Tower, according to a source familiar with his plans.

The Secret Service is scheduled to accompany Trump in the early afternoon Tuesday to the district attorney’s office, which is in the same building as the courthouse, where he is expected to be arraigned.
The former president is expected to return to Florida shortly after his court appearance and has scheduled an event that evening to speak publicly.
Lawyers for former President Donald Trump told a New York judge on Monday that they oppose the request by media outlets to broadcast Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday.

“We submit that the media request should be denied because it will create a circus-like atmosphere at the arraignment, raise unique security concerns, and is inconsistent with President Trump’s presumption of innocence,” the Trump team said in a letter to New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchant.
Trump’s attorneys said in their letter to Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan that he is required under court rules to take into account potential security concerns.
Among the Trump lawyers signing the new letter was Todd Blanche, who, CNN reported, recently joined the former president’s legal team.
Meanwhile, the Manhattan District Attorney’s office also responded Monday to the news outlets’ request, and said that it was deferring to the judge to decide how best to manage his court room.

However, the district attorney’s office wrote that it would “be a defensible exercise of the Court’s discretion to exclude or restrict videography, photography, and radio coverage of the arraignment in the interest of avoiding potential prejudice to the defendant, maintaining an orderly proceeding, assuring the safety of the participants in the proceeding, or for other reasons within the Court’s broad authority to manage and control these proceedings.”
But the prosecutors also noted that there “does not appear to be a categorical prohibition on cameras during an arraignment” under existing New York statutes and case law.

While the district attorney’s office stopped short of opposing the request, its lawyer pointed out to Merchan that a similar request for audio-video broadcasting was made for the 2021 arraignment in the tax fraud case against Trump Organization and its CFO Allen Weisselberg.
The judge responded to that 2021 request by “allowing a limited number of still photographs to be taken prior to the commencement of proceedings,” the prosecutors noted Monday.
CNN is one of the outlets requesting camera access for Tuesday’s arraignment.
Former President Donald Trump has hired a new attorney to serve as lead counsel in his defense against charges brought by the Manhattan district attorney’s office, multiple sources tell CNN.

Trump has hired Todd Blanche, who was most recently a partner at law firm Cadwalader, Wickersham & Taft. Blanche has previously represented Trump campaign manager Paul Manafort and Igor Fruman, a former associate of Rudy Giuliani who was also a key figure in Trump’s first impeachment trial. Politico was first to report the news of Blanche’s hiring.
Trump attorney’s Joe Tacopina and Susan Necheles will remain on Trump’s legal team.

Blanche’s hiring has been seen by some inside Trump’s orbit as a sidelining of Tacopina, who up until this point has been one of the most forward-facing attorney’s dealing with Trump’s defense. However, a senior adviser to Trump pushed back on that characterization and said the addition of Blanche was intended to add more legal firepower to Trump’s defense.

When pressed by CNN’s Kaitlan Collins on Friday if Tacopina was the right lawyer in New York to take Trump to trial, another lawyer representing the former president, Tim Parlatore, pointed to a potential conflict of interest.

“I know that Joe has certain potential conflict issues, given his prior contacts, with Stormy Daniels. So, who’s the right attorney, to take it to trial, is something that the client will have to decide. Ultimately, the decision of who to stand next to, before a jury, is a decision that only the client can make,” Parlatore said.
Asked by CNN’s Paula Reid if he is still on the case and whether he will be in court tomorrow, Tacopina said: “Yes of course ! And I will be the lead trial lawyer when the bell rings!”
CNN’s Paula Reid contributed reporting to this post.
Senate Homeland Security Chairman Gary Peters said he has not seen any indication that protests in Washington, DC, over former President Donald Trump’s indictment will become dangerous.
“I think you’re always going to be vigilant, so folks will be vigilant. Security and local law enforcement are certainly monitoring it,” he told reporters Monday.

Peters, who is also a member of Senate Democrat leadership, said it is unclear what effect the indictment will have on the Senate. “We don’t know what’s gonna transpire tomorrow, let alone what’s going to happen in the few weeks and months. I think we’d have to take a look at what the indictment is all about.”
Former President Donald Trump has departed Florida and is en route to New York to face criminal charges.
His personalized Boeing 757 took off from the Palm Beach International Airport this afternoon at about 12:59 p.m. ET ahead of his Tuesday appearance in a Manhattan courtroom to be arraigned.

Trump, the first current or former president to face criminal charges in American history, is expected to land at New York’s LaGuardia airport around 3 p.m. ET, according to a source familiar with his plans. He will stay at Trump Tower tonight, the source told CNN.

Trump faces more than 30 counts related to business fraud, according to two sources familiar with the case. A New York grand jury handed down the sealed indictment late last week. The charges have yet to be made public.

The former president is not expected to stay in New York City for very long. Immediately after his Tuesday court appearance, Trump plans to return to Florida, the source said, where he has scheduled an event to speak publicly.
Track Trump’s plane from Florida to New York here.
CNN’s Alta D. Spells and Jack Forrest contributed reporting to this post.

New York City Mayor Eric Adams warned GOP Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene to “be on your best behavior” after the Republican firebrand said she will travel to the city to protest former President Donald Trump’s indictment.
Adams made the statement at a press conference as New York security officials detailed plans ahead of Trump’s arrival in Manhattan for his arraignment scheduled on Tuesday.

“While there may be some rabble rousers thinking about coming to our city tomorrow, our message is clear and simple: Control yourselves. New York City is our home, not a playground for your misplaced anger. We have the safest large city in America because we respect the rule of law in New York City. And although we have no specific threats, people like Marjorie Taylor Greene, who is known to spread misinformation and hate speech — she stated she is coming to town. While you’re in town, be on your best behavior,” Adams said.

“As always, we will not allow violence or vandalism of any kind. And if one is caught participating in any act of violence, they will be arrested and held accountable. No matter who you are,” he added.

title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
summary: A female suspect has been detained in connection with an explosion that killed a prominent Russian military blogger at a cafe in St. Petersburg on Sunday.
paragraphs: The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.
The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.
It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.
“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.
West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”
Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.
He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.
“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.
He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”
Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.
Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

title: Jury shown CCTV of Huntingdon train staff using frying pan in defence
summary: A train crew member shows "sheer courage and bravery in seeking to save lives", a court hears.
paragraphs: CCTV shows frying pan used to stop train attacker
CCTV footage of a crew member using a frying pan to fend off a knifeman aboard a train has been shown in court.

Prosecutor Christopher Paxton KC said Samir Zitouni showed "sheer courage and bravery in seeking to save lives and defend others", during the mass stabbing on the Doncaster to London King's Cross train.
Jurors at Cambridge Crown Court saw footage of Zitouni using the pan against Anthony Williams, before the train made an unscheduled stop at Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire, on 1 November 2025.
Williams, 33, of Langford Road, Peterborough, denies attempting to murder 10 people aboard the train, three people in Peterborough the day before and a boy at a London railway station.
The trial has been told that whether Williams carried out the attacks was not in question, but jurors must consider whether he intended to kill those individuals.
On the second day of the trial, Paxton told jurors the attack on Zitouni was "prolonged, persistent and brutal".
Zitouni was said to have told the defendant: "We love you, we can help you."
Other CCTV footage played in court showed people fleeing the train.
Zitouni, in what Paxton called a "blood-soaked shirt", appeared "to be one of the last off the train", and Paxton said he fell "between, essentially, the gap between the train and the platform".
The court heard both of Zitouni's lungs had been punctured and he needed four blood transfusions, chest drains and the assistance of a ventilator.
Paxton earlier said one of the passengers, Raza Aslam, had grabbed a frying pan, but was stabbed in the hand by Williams.
He said Zitouni started throwing things at the defendant and "saved" Aslam's life.
Jurors also heard that Aslam told police Williams "had the greatest delight on his face".
Aslam said: "I saw his eyes expand with pleasure. I saw the contempt on his face, like a person who's high.
"He was just loving every single moment. He loved seeing us in desperation."
Paxton also told the jury how there was hand-to-hand fighting on the train.
He said Sachin Balakrishnan was stabbed in the forearm and chest, which punctured a lung and was "just centimetres from his heart".
The jury heard a call Stephen Crean made to 999 from a locked toilet on the train, telling the operator he had been stabbed "all over" and left "covered in blood".
Commenting on CCTV footage, Paxton said: "You can see the panic, you can see the fear in the faces of those fleeing.
"In this storm of violence, and even when gripped by fear, many there on that train helped others and, as we will see, some stood tall, quite literally, against the defendant's violent onslaught."
Jurors also heard how Scott Green had been travelling on the train with his dog, Poppy.
Paxton said: "He thought he was going to lose his life on the train when the defendant tried to stab him for the third time.
"It seems, members of the jury, that Poppy the dog, for Mr Green at least, saved the day and sent the defendant running off.
"You will hear that in an unrelated incident the defendant had previously been bitten by a dog."
Following the trial of Anthony Williams from Peterborough who is accused of carrying out multiple stabbing attacks on a train in Cambridgeshire in 2025, and separate attacks.
During Thursday's evidence, the court was also told of an attack on 73-year-old David Presland, who had been stabbed in the back while on his hands and knees.
Presland said he had been "helped by someone he knew as Kevin" - believed to be Kevin Deely, another of those Williams is accused of attempting to murder.
Paxton told the court the events were "all over in about five minutes", adding: "In that time, 10 men are stabbed by one man, this defendant, Mr Williams."

Williams is accused of attempting to murder Aslam, Balakrishnan, Crean, Deely, Green, Presland and Zitouni on the train between Peterborough and Huntingdon on the Saturday evening, along with Scott Bletcher, Jonathan Gjoshe and Michael Paffett.

He is also accused of attempting to murder a 14-year-old boy and Dawid Taborski on a footbridge near Henry Penn Walk in Peterborough on 31 October, and William Ogelby at Railworld car park in the city shortly afterwards.

Zitouni, in what Paxton called a "blood-soaked shirt", appeared "to be one of the last off the train", and Paxton said he fell "between, essentially, the gap between the train and the platform".

title: Στα 5 δισ. δολάρια εκτοξεύθηκαν τα έσοδα της FIFA από εισιτήρια-πακέτα φιλοξενίας στο Μουντιάλ 2026
summary: Στα 5 δισεκατομμύρια δολάρια εκτοξεύθηκαν τα καθαρά έσοδα της FIFA, από το Μουντιάλ 2026. Αιτία αυτών των θετικών αποτελεσμάτων για την Διεθνή Ομοσπονδία φέρεται να είναι η δυναμική τιμολόγηση στα...Περισσότερα...
paragraphs: Στα 5 δισ. δολάρια εκτοξεύθηκαν τα έσοδα της FIFA από εισιτήρια-πακέτα φιλοξενίας στο Μουντιάλ 2026

Στα 5 δισεκατομμύρια δολάρια εκτοξεύθηκαν τα καθαρά έσοδα της FIFA, από το Μουντιάλ 2026. Αιτία αυτών των θετικών αποτελεσμάτων για την Διεθνή Ομοσπονδία φέρεται να είναι η δυναμική τιμολόγηση στα εισιτήρια, τα πακέτα φιλοξενίας κατά την διάρκεια της παγκόσμιας διοργάνωσης αλλά και οι επιπλέον 40 αγώνες που διεξήχθησαν στο Μουντιάλ.

Ο προέδρος της FIFA, Τζιάνι Ινφαντίνο, πριν από λίγες ημέρες είχε ανακοινώσει ότι το φετινό Παγκόσμιο Κύπελλο ποδοσφαίρου που συνδιοργανώθηκε από ΗΠΑ, Καναδά, Μεξικό απέφερε συνολικά έσοδοα 15 δισεκατομμυρίων δολαρίων, πόσο μεγαλύτερο κατά δύο δισεκατομμύρια από τις αρχικές εκτιμήσεις των ανθρώπων της Διεθνούς Ομοσπονδίας Ποδοσφαίρου.
Το ποσό των 5 δισ δολαρίων είναι υπερπενταπλάσιο από τα αντίστοιχα έσοδα που είχαν παραχθεί από τη διοργάνωση στο Κατάρ πριν από τέσσερα χρόνια.

Υπενθυμίζεται ότι το Παγκόσμιο Κύπελλο του 2026 περιλάμβανε 40 επιπλέον αγώνες -συνολικά 104- σε σύγκριση με το Κατάρ (64), όπου οι πωλήσεις εισιτηρίων και πακέτων φιλοξενίας το 2022 είχαν αποφέρει έσοδα 929 εκατομμυρίων δολαρίων.
Η θύελλα αντιδράσεων στη FIFA για την τιμολογιακή πολιτική

Αξίζει να σημειωθεί ότι η διοικούσα αρχή της FIFA είχε στόχος σφοδρής κριτικής για την τιμολογιακή της πολιτική στη φετινή διοργάνωση, αφού εφάρμοσε για πρώτη φορά δυναμική τιμολόγηση και παρακρατούσε προμήθεια 30% σε κάθε μεταπώληση.

Μάλιστα η Football Supporters Europe και ο οργανισμός προστασίας καταναλωτών Euroconsumers είχαν καταθέσει επίσημη καταγγελία στην Ευρωπαϊκή Επιτροπή, για τις αστρονομικές τιμές όπως τις είχαν χαρακτηρίσει.

Από την πλευρά της η FIFA υπερασπίστηκε επανειλημμένα τις τιμές υποστηρίζοντας ότι όλα τα έσοδα από τις πωλήσεις θα επανεπενδυθούν τελικά στο ποδόσφαιρο, σημειώνοντας παράλληλα ότι αντικατόπτριζαν την αγορά της Βόρειας Αμερικής, όπου η καταβολή εκατοντάδων δολαρίων για την παρακολούθηση αθλητικών γεγονότων είναι σύνηθες φαινόμενο.

«Τα έσοδα που παρήχθησαν από τη διοργάνωση θα προσφέρουν πρωτοφανείς πόρους στις Ομοσπονδίες-Μέλη της FIFA για να επενδύσουν στο άθλημα, υποστηρίζοντας την ανάπτυξη του ανδρικού, γυναικείου και αναπτυξιακού ποδοσφαίρου και στις 211 ομοσπονδίες-μέλη, κάθε μέρα του χρόνου», δήλωσε εκπρόσωπος της FIFA.

«Όπως ανακοινώθηκε νωρίτερα αυτόν τον μήνα μετά τη συνεδρίαση του Συμβουλίου της FIFA στη Ζυρίχη, παρουσιάστηκε η πρωτοβουλία «FIFA Surplus Solidarity Programme», η οποία θα χρησιμοποιήσει μέρος των αποθεματικών της FIFA για να υπερδιπλασιάσει την προγραμματισμένη χρηματοδότηση για την περίοδο 2027-2030, φτάνοντας τα 6,35 δισεκατομμύρια δολάρια».

title: Πέθανε ο ηθοποιός Πάτρικ Στιούαρτ των «Star Trek» και «X-Men»
summary: Εφυγε από τη ζωή σε ηλικία 86 ετών ο εμβληματικός ηθοποιός Πάτρικ Στιούαρτ που έγινε γνωστός από τους ρόλους του στα Star Trek και X-MenΠερισσότερα...
paragraphs: Πέθανε ο ηθοποιός Πάτρικ Στιούαρτ των «Star Trek» και «X-Men»
Εφυγε από τη ζωή σε ηλικία 86 ετών ο εμβληματικός ηθοποιός Πάτρικ Στιούαρτ που έγινε γνωστός από τους ρόλους του στα Star Trek και X-Men

Ο Στιούαρτ πέθανε την Τετάρτη στο σπίτι του στο Λος Άντζελες μετά από «ένα σύντομο και συγκινητικό ταξίδι με τη νόσο Αλτσχάιμερ και την άνοια», όπως ανακοίνωσε η επί χρόνια εκπρόσωπός του, Κέλι Μπους Νόβακ.

«Βρισκόταν στη ζεστή αγκαλιά της οικογένειας και των φίλων του, περιτριγυρισμένος από ζωντανή μουσική, προσευχή, δάκρυα, γέλιο και το είδος του βαθιού συναισθήματος που μόνο εκείνος θα μπορούσε να εμπνεύσει μετά από μια ζωή γεμάτη αφοσίωση σε όλους μας», έγραψε η Μπους Νόβακ. «Θα κρατάμε για πάντα στην καρδιά μας τη γαλήνια ηρεμία και την αντανάκλαση στο πρόσωπό του, μια παντοτινή υπενθύμιση της ανίκητης χάρης του».

Ο Πάτρικ Στιούαρτ στο «Star Trek» The Next Generation ταυτίστηκε απόλυτα με τον ρόλο του Πλοιάρχου Ζαν-Λουκ Πικάρντ ενώ ενσάρκωσε μοναδικά τον Καθηγητή Τσαρλς Εξέιβιερ (Professor X) στη διάσημη κινηματογραφική σειρά υπερηρώων «X-Men».
Ήταν σαιξπηρικός ηθοποιός πριν κατακτήσει το Χόλιγουντ, αφού είχε μια λαμπρή, πολυετή καριέρα στο κλασικό θέατρο της Βρετανίας και στο Royal Shakespeare Company.

title: Flávio Bolsonaro calls himself 'leader of Brazil' after election loss
summary: The defeated presidential candidate says he will lead the opposition from the US.
paragraphs: Flávio Bolsonaro calls himself 'leader of Brazil' after election loss

The defeated candidate in Brazil's presidential election, Flávio Bolsonaro, has referred to himself as "leader of Brazil" in a letter he published on social media after leaving the country for the United States.
Bolsonaro lost to his left-wing rival, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, in the run-off on Sunday by a difference of 4.4 million votes, but has not conceded defeat.
In the letter, Bolsonaro alleges, without offering evidence, that he was the victim of "electoral fraud" and says that he will lead the opposition from the US.
He left Brazil on Tuesday after failing to comply with an order to surrender his passports, a decision which Lula described as "a shameful act".
Bolsonaro starts his letter, which he posted on his X account, saying "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the leader of Brazil".
However, he had posted a previous version, that was later deleted, in which he wrote: "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the rightful president of Brazil."
Both versions repeat the allegation that Bolsonaro first made on election night, that an extension of polling hours on Sunday had benefited his rival.
In the letter, he says it was "an electoral fraud unfolding before my eyes".

The extension was requested by both Lula's and Bolsonaro's campaign teams, and the head of Brazil's electoral authority has said that the vote proceeded normally and in full accordance with the country's laws and constitution.

An analysis of election data conducted by BBC Brazil and BBC Verify has also found that only around 34,000 people voted during the extended hours - far lower than the 4.4 million votes that separated Lula from Bolsonaro.
In his letter, Bolsonaro also addresses his departure from Brazil - which caused confusion after he disappeared for more than 24 hours.
It later emerged that he had gone across the land border to Argentina, and from there flew on to Florida, following a brief refuelling stop in Ecuador.
Bolsonaro left after failing to hand in his passports to police - in defiance of a Supreme Court order, which had been issued as part of an investigation into alleged money laundering.
He has not been charged as part of the money laundering probe and denies any wrongdoing, calling the investigation a "politically-motivated witch hunt".
Bolsonaro added that he had never intended to leave Brazil, but argued that he was the victim of "political persecution".
He ended the letter by saying: "I left Brazil but I haven't abandoned Brazilians".
While Flávio Bolsonaro said that he planned to lead the opposition from the US, it was not clear how he planned to do that.

His party recognised the election result and while some of its politicians have described Bolsonaro as a "political exile", his campaign manager, Rogério Marinho, stated on Wednesday that "there is no evidence" of the electoral fraud that Bolsonaro alleges took place.
It is also not yet clear where Bolsonaro intends to stay or for how long.

His younger brother, Eduardo, has been in self-imposed exile in the US since March 2025, saying he was the victim of political persecution. The two siblings posted a photo of themselves holding a Brazilian flag on Wednesday.
The Trump administration has provided visas for Flávio Bolsonaro and his family but did not say what kind of visas they were.
The US president did not explicitly endorse Bolsonaro in the run-up to the election and told reporters he "won't get involved" when asked about Bolsonaro's allegations of election fraud.
Earlier in the week, he had said that "it looked like another rigged election," without providing any evidence.
And on Thursday, Trump told reporters that "the election was a very great embarrassment to the people of Brazil".
body:
The defeated candidate in Brazil's presidential election, Flávio Bolsonaro, has referred to himself as "leader of Brazil" in a letter he published on social media after leaving the country for the United States.

Bolsonaro lost to his left-wing rival, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, in the run-off on Sunday by a difference of 4.4 million votes, but has not conceded defeat.

In the letter, Bolsonaro alleges, without offering evidence, that he was the victim of "electoral fraud" and says that he will lead the opposition from the US.

He left Brazil on Tuesday after failing to comply with an order to surrender his passports, a decision which Lula described as "a shameful act".

Bolsonaro starts his letter, which he posted on his X account, saying "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the leader of Brazil".

However, he had posted a previous version, that was later deleted, in which he wrote: "I address the Brazilian people and the international community as the rightful president of Brazil."

Both versions repeat the allegation that Bolsonaro first made on election night, that an extension of polling hours on Sunday had benefited his rival.

In the letter, he says it was "an electoral fraud unfolding before my eyes".

The extension was requested by both Lula's and Bolsonaro's campaign teams, and the head of Brazil's electoral authority has said that the vote proceeded normally and in full accordance with the country's laws…

title: Νέα τηλεφωνική επικοινωνία Τραμπ - Ερντογάν μέσα σε ένα 24ωρο για τη Σύνοδο της Άγκυρας
summary: Οι πρόεδροι της Τουρκίας και των ΗΠΑ, Ρετζέπ Ταγίπ Ερντογάν και Ντόναλντ Τραμπ είχαν τη δεύτερη τηλεφωνική επικοινωνία τους μέσα σε ένα 24ωρο.Περισσότερα...
paragraphs: Νέα τηλεφωνική επικοινωνία Τραμπ - Ερντογάν μέσα σε ένα 24ωρο για τη Σύνοδο της Άγκυρας
Οι πρόεδροι της Τουρκίας και των ΗΠΑ, Ρετζέπ Ταγίπ Ερντογάν και Ντόναλντ Τραμπ είχαν τη δεύτερη τηλεφωνική επικοινωνία τους μέσα σε ένα 24ωρο.
Αυτή τη φορά οι δύο πρόεδροι επικοινώνησαν με αφορμή τη σύνοδο κορυφής του Οργανισμού Τουρκογενών Κρατών που πρόκειται να πραγματοποιηθεί στην 'Αγκυρα.

Σύμφωνα με ανακοίνωση της διεύθυνσης επικοινωνίας της τουρκικής προεδρίας, ο Αμερικανός πρόεδρος τηλεφώνησε στον Ρετζέπ Ταγίπ Ερντογάν κατά τη διάρκεια επίσημου δείπνου που παρατέθηκε παρουσία ξένων ηγετών για την εθνική επέτειο της ίδρυσης της Τουρκικής Δημοκρατίας, στις 29 Οκτωβρίου.

Κατά τη συνομιλία, ο Ταγίπ Ερντογάν μετέφερε στον Τραμπ τους χαιρετισμούς των ηγετών που συμμετείχαν στο δείπνο και αναφέρθηκε στη σημασία της επικείμενης 13ης Συνόδου Κορυφής του Οργανισμού Τουρκογενών Κρατών.

Όπως ανακοίνωσε η τουρκική προεδρία, ο Ερντογάν επισήμανε ότι στη Σύνοδο της 'Αγκυρας θα ληφθούν αποφάσεις για την περαιτέρω ενίσχυση του Οργανισμού, ο οποίος, με συνολικό πληθυσμό που υπερβαίνει τα 200 εκατομμύρια, έχει εξελιχθεί, κατά την εκτίμησή του, σε σημείο αναφοράς για τη σταθερότητα και την ασφάλεια στην Κεντρική Ασία.
Από την πλευρά του, ο Ντόναλντ Τραμπ ευχήθηκε στον Τούρκο πρόεδρο κάθε επιτυχία στις εργασίες της συνόδου κορυφής.

Η νέα επικοινωνία ακολούθησε τη χθεσινή τηλεφωνική συνομιλία των δύο προέδρων κατά την οποία, σύμφωνα με την 'Αγκυρα, συζητήθηκαν οι διμερείς σχέσεις, οι εξελίξεις στη Μέση Ανατολή και ο πόλεμος στην Ουκρανία.

title: Grealish dropped by Everton after 'breach of club discipline'
summary: Jack Grealish is left out of Everton's Carabao Cup tie with Newcastle United on Thursday "due to a breach of club discipline".
paragraphs: Grealish dropped by Everton after 'breach of club discipline'
Jack Grealish was left out of Everton's Carabao Cup tie with Newcastle United on Thursday "due to a breach of club discipline"., external
Everton did not disclose any further details but it is believed it was for missing a training session.
England winger Grealish, 31, is on loan at Everton from Premier League rivals Manchester City.

He spent a large chunk of last season with the Toffees under a similar arrangement, scoring twice and providing six assists in 20 appearances, before sustaining a season-ending foot injury in January.
Grealish came on as a substitute during City's 3-0 Community Shield defeat to Arsenal at Wembley in August.
The former Aston Villa player, who cost City £100m in 2021, also featured as a substitute during City's 2-1 win over Bournemouth on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.
He returned to Everton before the transfer window closed and has featured five times for them this season in the Premier League.
Grealish also played in Everton's Carabao Cup third round win over Wolves.

title: Ακαδημία Πλάτωνος: Δεν βρέθηκαν εγκλωβισμένοι μετά την κατάρρευση στέγης παλαιού κτηρίου
summary: Χωρίς να βρεθούν εγκλωβισμένα άτομα ολοκληρώθηκε η επιχείρηση της πυροσβεστικής μετά την κατάρρευση τμήματος εγκαταλελειμμένου κτηρίου στην περιοχή της Ακαδημίας Πλάτωνος. Περισσότερα...
paragraphs: Ακαδημία Πλάτωνος: Δεν βρέθηκαν εγκλωβισμένοι μετά την κατάρρευση στέγης παλαιού κτηρίου
Χωρίς να βρεθούν εγκλωβισμένα άτομα ολοκληρώθηκε η επιχείρηση της πυροσβεστικής μετά την κατάρρευση τμήματος εγκαταλελειμμένου κτηρίου στην περιοχή της Ακαδημίας Πλάτωνος.
Από το οίκημα, που βρίσκεται επί της Αλαμάνας 108, κατέρρευσαν η σκεπή και μέρος της τοιχοποιίας.
Όπως έγινε γνωστό από την πυροσβεστική, κατά τη διάρκεια της επιχείρησης έρευνας και διάσωσης δεν εντοπίστηκαν εγκλωβισμένοι.
Ειδικότερα το Κέντρο Επιχειρήσεων του Πυροσβεστικού Σώματος ενημερώθηκε περίπου στις 11:20 για κατάρρευση στέγης και μέρος της τοιχοποιίας εγκαταλελειμμένης μονοκατοικίας.
Καρέ καρέ η επιχείρηση της Πυροσβεστικής μετά την κατάρρευση
Στο σημείο κινητοποιήθηκαν 17 πυροσβέστες με 5 οχήματα και ειδικό διασωστικό όχημα της 1ης ΕΜΑΚ, καθώς και ένας σκύλος έρευνας και διάσωσης, αλλά και δυνάμεις της ΕΛΑΣ.

Όπως έγινε γνωστό από την πυροσβεστική, στο σημείο του συμβάντος πραγματοποιήθηκαν όλες οι προβλεπόμενες ενέργειες για τον έλεγχο του χώρου, ενώ κινητοποιήθηκε κι ο δήμος Αθηναίων για την μεταφορά αδρανών υλικών εφόσον απαιτηθεί.
Για την διερεύνηση των αιτίων του συμβάντος κινητοποιήθηκε το ανακριτικό κλιμάκιο αντιμετώπισης εγκλημάτων εμπρησμού Αθηνών.
Δείτε βίντεο του CNN Greece από την επιχείρηση της Πυροσβεστικής:
«Δεν ήμουν εδώ. Ξέρω ότι αυτό το σπίτι είναι ακατοίκητο πάρα πολλά χρόνια και δεν ενδιαφέρεται κανείς για την ανοικοδόμησή του.

Είχαν γίνει καταγγελίες για το γεγονός ότι μπαινοέβγαιναν μέσα άστεγοι. Πάρα πολλά κτίσματα στην γειτονιά είναι ακατοίκητα στην γειτονιά, περίπου 40 χρόνια» τόνισε, μεταξύ άλλων, κάτοικος της περιοχής.

title: Paris suburb shooting suspect targeted people of Muslim or African appearance, prosecutor says
summary: Kevin T has been charged with murder and attempted murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise.
paragraphs: Paris suburb shooting suspect targeted people of Muslim or African appearance, prosecutor says
A man suspected of a deadly shooting near Paris last week has admitted targeting people of "Muslim, African or North African" appearance, prosecutors say.
A man was killed and seven people including a child were injured last Friday when an attacker opened fire as he drove through two western suburbs.
On Thursday the suspect was charged with murder and attempted murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise, the national anti-terrorism prosecutor's office (PNAT) said.
President Emmanuel Macron called it a "racist terrorist attack" and anti-racism demonstrations have been held around France.
Pengo Bossio Wangi, a 26-year-old French-Congolese martial artist, was killed in the shooting.
Three of those wounded were still in hospital with one in critical condition, terrorism prosecutor Olivier Christen told reporters.
The suspect, named in French media as 39-year-old Kevin T, chose Trappes and nearby La Verrière because he saw them as a "hotbed for Islamists", he said.
Kevin T had denied any "terrorist intent", insisted his actions were "legitimate" and said he "feels no regret", Christen said.

Police found "weapons or weapon components" in the suspect's home as well as books including a Quran, a Bible and Adolf Hitler's Mein Kampf and stickers celebrating the hard-right National Rally (RN) party, Christen said.
Kevin T told investigators that he had designed the stickers with slogans such as "long live France, RN, proud to be French" himself and had them printed more than a year ago, Christen said.
But the suspect also told investigators he was not a member or supporter of any political party.
On Wednesday Macron said that "certain political movements on the far right" including the RN and "those close to them" had allowed a climate of racism "to take root".
Jean-Philippe Tanguy, a prominent RN lawmaker, retorted that it was the president himself who had allowed "hateful ideologies" to flourish.
France's presidential elections is six months away and RN leader Marine Le Pen is currently leading opinion polls.
body:
A man suspected of a deadly shooting near Paris last week has admitted targeting people of "Muslim, African or North African" appearance, prosecutors say.

A man was killed and seven people including a child were injured last Friday when an attacker opened fire as he drove through two western suburbs.

On Thursday the suspect was charged with murder and attempted murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise, the national anti-terrorism prosecutor's office (PNAT) said.

President Emmanuel Macron called it a "racist terrorist attack" and anti-racism demonstrations have been held around France.

Pengo Bossio Wangi, a 26-year-old French-Congolese martial artist, was killed in the shooting.

Three of those wounded were still in hospital with one in critical condition, terrorism prosecutor Olivier Christen told reporters.

The suspect, named in French media as 39-year-old Kevin T, chose Trappes and nearby La Verrière because he saw them as a "hotbed for Islamists", he said.

Kevin T had denied any "terrorist intent", insisted his actions were "legitimate" and said he "feels no regret", Christen said.

Police found "weapons or weapon components" in the suspect's home as well as books including a Quran, a Bible and Adolf Hitler's Mein Kampf and stickers celebrating the hard-right National Rally (RN) party, Christen said.

Kevin T told investigators that he had designed the stickers with slogans such as "long live France, RN, proud to be French" himself and had them printed more than a year ago, Christen said.
