title: Tesla Just Gained 13% in a Month: Take Profits, or Buy More?
summary: Key TakeawaysTesla stock is up 13% in the past month on a delivery beat, SpaceX merger talk, a Barclays upgrade and robotaxi news. Much of the gain rests on a SpaceX deal that has no terms yet, while Tesla’s third-quarter profit fell from a year ago.
paragraphs: - Tesla stock is up 13% in the past month on a delivery beat, SpaceX merger talk, a Barclays upgrade and robotaxi news.
- Much of the gain rests on a SpaceX deal that has no terms yet, while Tesla’s third-quarter profit fell from a year ago.
- Tesla’s forward P/E is far above its five-year average, and consensus earnings through 2028 stay below what Tesla earned in 2022.
- Buying more makes sense only once the two companies’ special committees put a real premium on paper, and the Dallas Cybercab launch in November is the next marker.
Tesla (TSLA) stock is up 13% in the past month, while the S&P 500 barely moved and the Nasdaq 100 slipped.
Most of that came from talk that SpaceX (SPCX) will buy the company, and from robotaxi news that hasn’t reached Tesla’s earnings.
Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, it said before the open on Oct. 2: down 2% from a year ago, but up from the second quarter and well above the roughly 461,000 analysts expected.

Barclays analyst Dan Levy sketched an all-stock deal, with SpaceX as the buyer, on Oct. 14. On SpaceX’s Oct. 20 call, Elon Musk said both companies had formed special committees of independent directors to weigh a merger, and called one “a good idea.”

On Oct. 26, Levy upgraded Tesla to Overweight and raised his target to $450 from $370. He cited the auto business, Megapacks and robotaxis, but the deal leads his case: “We believe the anticipated merger is now a key part of the Tesla bull case.”
There are no terms yet. A Tesla vote would need a majority of all outstanding shares, a bar Musk himself called high, and the agenda for Tesla’s Dec. 3 annual meeting carries no merger item.

In Levy’s all-stock sketch, Tesla holders would be paid in SpaceX stock. SpaceX’s third-quarter revenue jumped 161% to $14.6 billion, but Barclays, citing Bloomberg consensus, has it burning $17 billion of free cash flow in 2030 while Tesla brings in $12 billion.
TIKR tracks 45 analysts on Tesla. How many say “Buy”?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Tesla, along with Wall Street’s revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Tesla’s Analyst Ratings

Tesla’s own third-quarter report, out after the close on Oct. 21, was less exciting. Revenue was flat at $28.05 billion. GAAP net income fell to $787 million from $1.37 billion, and free cash flow to $1.53 billion from $3.99 billion.

Adjusted EPS of $0.48 beat estimates, the car backlog hit a four-year high, and active FSD subscriptions rose to 1.74 million from 1.04 million. But management cut its 2026 capex plan to about $20 billion from more than $25 billion, and Musk said Optimus is at least a year from making 20,000 robots a week.

After the close on Oct. 26, ARK Invest reaffirmed its $4,400 price target for 2031, with about 80% of Tesla’s value that year tied to robotaxis. Musk posted “A Storm of Cybercabs” on X overnight, and Tesla said its Texas plant now turns out Cybercabs faster than it can deploy them.
Deploying them is the hard part. On the third-quarter call, management counted six Robotaxi cities. In January, Musk had expected driverless service in “dozens of major cities” by year-end.
The valuation already counts on a lot of this. Tesla traded at 190x forward earnings at the Oct. 27 close, against a five-year average of 108x:
Analysts expect normalized EPS to climb from $1.74 in 2026 to $3.20 in 2028, still below the $4.07 Tesla earned in 2022:
Musk expects robotaxi revenue to become noticeable only by the second quarter of 2027, so this month’s news shouldn’t move those numbers much.
And the stock ended the month right at Wall Street’s average target of $411:
My take: I wouldn’t buy more here, and trimming makes more sense than adding. Without a deal, Tesla has to hold that multiple on its own earnings, which fell last quarter.

A merger with a real premium would change the math. Until the committees put one on paper, the next markers are the Dallas Cybercab launch, which management set for November, and fourth-quarter deliveries in early January.

paragraphs: Χρησιμοποιούμε cookie και δεδομένα, συμπεριλαμβανομένων των διευθύνσεων IP, για:
- Την παροχή και τη συντήρηση των υπηρεσιών Google
- Την παρακολούθηση διακοπών λειτουργίας και την προστασία από ανεπιθύμητο περιεχόμενο και φαινόμενα απάτης και κατάχρησης
- Τη μέτρηση της αφοσίωσης του κοινού και την παροχή στατιστικών στοιχείων ιστοτόπων, για να κατανοήσουμε πώς χρησιμοποιούνται οι υπηρεσίες μας και να βελτιώσουμε την ποιότητά τους
- Την ανάπτυξη και τη βελτίωση νέων υπηρεσιών
- Την προβολή διαφημίσεων και τη μέτρηση της αποτελεσματικότητάς τους
- Την εμφάνιση εξατομικευμένου περιεχομένου, ανάλογα με τις ρυθμίσεις σας
- Την εμφάνιση εξατομικευμένων διαφημίσεων, ανάλογα με τις ρυθμίσεις σας
Εάν επιλέξετε "Απόρριψη όλων", δεν θα χρησιμοποιούμε cookie ή διευθύνσεις IP για αυτούς τους πρόσθετους σκοπούς.

Το μη εξατομικευμένο περιεχόμενο επηρεάζεται από παράγοντες όπως το περιεχόμενο που βλέπετε εκείνη τη στιγμή, τη δραστηριότητά σας στην ενεργή περίοδο λειτουργίας αναζήτησης και την τοποθεσία σας. Οι μη εξατομικευμένες διαφημίσεις επηρεάζονται από το περιεχόμενο που βλέπετε εκείνη τη στιγμή και τη γενική τοποθεσία σας. Στο εξατομικευμένο περιεχόμενο και τις διαφημίσεις ενδέχεται επίσης να περιλαμβάνονται πιο συναφή αποτελέσματα, προτάσεις καθώς και προσαρμοσμένες διαφημίσεις βάσει της προηγούμενης δραστηριότητας σε αυτό το πρόγραμμα περιήγησης, όπως προηγούμενες αναζητήσεις στην Google. Επίσης, χρησιμοποιούμε cookie και δεδομένα για να προσαρμόσουμε την εμπειρία των χρηστών προκειμένου να είναι κατάλληλη για τις συγκεκριμένες ηλικίες, εάν αυτό είναι απαραίτητο.

Επιλέξτε Περισσότερες επιλογές για να δείτε περισσότερες πληροφορίες, όπως λεπτομέρειες σχετικά με τη διαχείριση των ρυθμίσεων απορρήτου σας. Μπορείτε επίσης να επισκεφτείτε τη διεύθυνση g.co/privacytools ανά πάσα στιγμή.

title: Founder-Led Giants Redefining Technology and Global Market Growth
summary: NVIDIA, Dell, Shopify, Salesforce and BlackRock stand out as founder-run companies with strong vision, innovation and long-term growth drivers.
paragraphs: An updated edition of the Sept. 4, 2026, article.

Founders often play a pivotal role in shaping the strategic direction, corporate culture and long-term growth prospects of the businesses they establish. Their deep-rooted commitment and entrepreneurial vision often encourage them to embrace calculated risks, navigate challenges and explore opportunities that conventional management teams might overlook. As their leadership philosophies become embedded in business operations, founder-led companies can develop distinct competitive advantages that support sustainable growth. Currently, approximately 11% of large-cap U.S. companies are founder-led.

Despite accounting for less than 5% of the S&P 500, founder-led businesses wield considerable influence over the broader market. Visionary entrepreneurs such as Elon Musk, Warren Buffett, Steve Jobs, Jeff Bezos, Mark Zuckerberg and Bill Gates have reshaped industries and built globally recognized enterprises. Companies such as NVIDIA NVDA, Amazon, Meta Platforms, Tesla, Alphabet and Netflix demonstrate the lasting impact of entrepreneurial leadership and innovation. Together, these businesses represent nearly 15% of the S&P 500's market capitalization, with technology companies accounting for a significant portion.

Founder-driven businesses often emerge from innovative concepts designed to capitalize on technological advancements and evolving consumer needs. During their formative years, entrepreneurs frequently encounter investor skepticism and financing challenges, prompting them to rely on personal resources before securing external funding. As these enterprises mature, founders often retain substantial ownership stakes, aligning their financial interests with those of shareholders and encouraging a long-term approach to value creation.

However, founder-led companies also face certain challenges. Founders may be reluctant to delegate responsibilities or relinquish control over key decisions, potentially limiting operational flexibility and organizational expansion. While their direct involvement can preserve the company's original vision, excessive dependence on founder leadership may restrict access to specialized expertise and hinder scalability. Nevertheless, founder-led businesses have historically demonstrated impressive investment performance. According to a Motley Fool report, publicly traded companies managed by their founders delivered average annual returns of 25% over the past decade, outperforming the S&P 500's 14% return during the same period.

Our Founder-Run Companies Screen makes it easy to identify high-potential stocks. Currently, stocks like NVIDIA Corporation, Dell Technologies DELL, Shopify SHOP, Salesforce CRM and BlackRock Inc. BLK look appealing.

title: Is It Too Early To Buy American Airlines Stock?
summary: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.
paragraphs: Is It Too Early To Buy American Airlines Stock?
For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Shares of American Airlines (AAL) have fallen 18.5% over the past three months, while the S&P 500 gained 4.4%. At $12.58, the stock sits 30.7% below its July high, and a buyer who has waited for a lower price may think this is it. Yet the airline has grown its sales without growing its profit. Is $12.58 a low price for what American Airlines earns today?

American Airlines stock is cheap relative to sales, but the profit generated from those sales is low by its own history too. At the end of September, the shares traded at 0.145 times twelve months of sales. The stock was cheaper by that measure at only 7 of the 40 quarter ends since the end of 2016. The airline posted a 1.7% operating margin over those twelve months, compared to 4.2% a year earlier, and margins were lower at only 10 of those quarter ends.

After recording a net loss of $481 million over the past twelve months, the stock has no meaningful P/E. Shares also appear inexpensive against cash, trading at 2.0 times operating cash flow, though almost all of that cash arrived in the first quarter of 2026. Management says earnings, not financial deals, are the key to repairing its balance sheet, and earnings are where the damage shows.

Management attributes that damage to fuel. Higher fuel prices added $1.9 billion to costs in the third quarter. While sales rose 19.3% in the quarter, operating income fell to $124 million from $158 million a year earlier. So the stock is cheap against sales, but a net loss leaves no earnings for the price to look cheap against.
American Airlines Expects Another Loss In Its Fourth Quarter

Management expects fourth-quarter revenue to grow 19.5% to 22.5% from a year earlier. Analysts project fourth-quarter revenue of about $17.0 billion, a figure falling within management’s guidance. On last year’s fourth-quarter revenue of $14.0 billion, that guidance points to about $16.7 billion to $17.1 billion. So analysts expect American Airlines to deliver on that guidance, which forecasts another loss: an adjusted loss of $0.50 to $1.10 a share.
The pressure comes from fuel. Management expects fuel to cost about $4.70 a gallon on average in the quarter, up from the $3.85 the airline paid in the third quarter.

Management says demand is holding up. The airline’s managed corporate revenue rose 28% in the third quarter, marking its sixth straight quarter of double-digit growth, and total revenue came in above the high end of guidance. Management expects margins to widen meaningfully when fuel prices stabilize.

American Airlines is expected to report its fourth-quarter results in January 2027. Following recent reports, the stock has moved in both directions. Shares rose 10.3% in the two trading days after the July 2026 report, while they slipped 0.8% after the April 2026 report. Shares rose 10.3% in the two trading days after the July 2026 report, while they slipped 0.8% after the April 2026 report. After the October 22 report, shares fell 3.2% over the same two-day span.

The stock can also fall far during a market shock. Shares dropped 43% during the 2025 US Tariff Shock, compared to a 19% decline for the S&P 500. A buyer acting before January will hold the stock through any such shock that occurs in the meantime.

When American Airlines reports in January 2027, the two numbers to watch are its fourth-quarter revenue growth against its own guidance and the price paid per gallon of fuel. Until then, the stock is not cheap for what the airline earns, and the quarter covered by that report is guided to a loss.

Not necessarily on American Airlines alone, if your goal is long-term wealth. Wealth is built by owning the companies that keep outperforming, the leaders of their industries, wherever they are. Here are two companies from American Airlines’ own industry that have beaten it. Over the five years to October 2026, Delta Air Lines stock rose 113% and United Airlines stock rose 125%, while American Airlines stock fell 34%.

Finding companies like these takes comparison across industries and sectors, and that is what the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio does. It holds 30 quality companies in equal weight and, since its inception in September 2020, has returned more than 105%, ahead of a benchmark that combines the S&P 500, S&P Mid-cap and Russell 2000. See how we find the leaders.

title: AbbVie Stock: What 10 Years of Growth and Dividends Did for $1,000
summary: AbbVie built its empire on a single blockbuster drug, then watched biosimilars gut it almost overnight. Whether the replacement pipeline saved investors or left them holding the bag depends on when they bought and whether they had the nerve to stay.
paragraphs: AbbVie Stock: What 10 Years of Growth and Dividends Did for $1,000

AbbVie built its empire on a single blockbuster drug, then watched biosimilars gut it almost overnight. Whether the replacement pipeline saved investors or left them holding the bag depends on when they bought and whether they had the nerve to…

For AbbVie (NYSE:ABBV | ABBV Price Prediction), the last decade came down to one problem: life after Humira. AbbVie was spun off from Abbott Laboratories (NYSE:ABT) on January 1, 2013, and for years it relied on Humira, its flagship drug, for most of its cash flow. Humira lost U.S. exclusivity in early 2023, and biosimilars have taken a big share since. In Q2 2026, Humira sales fell 35.9% to $756M.

The replacement drugs arrived on time. Skyrizi grew 24.4% to $5.505B in Q2 2026, and Rinvoq rose 24.5% to $2.525B. The $63B Allergan deal, which closed in May 2020, brought in Botox, Vraylar, and an aesthetics business. Robert A. Michael took over as CEO in 2024. The pending $10.9B purchase of Apogee Therapeutics (NASDAQ:APGE) brings more depth to the immunology pipeline.

In 2016, AbbVie paid $0.57 per share each quarter. Today it pays $1.73, an increase of about 204%. The payout went up every year in the record, and the forward annual dividend now comes to $6.92, for a yield of roughly 2.30%. If you bought early and held, the cash you receive each year on your original investment has grown with every raise.
AbbVie’s figures include dividends. The S&P 500 figures, measured with the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY), count price gains only.

AbbVie beat the index over all three periods, and over 10 years it more than doubled the market’s price-only result. Part of that edge comes from reinvested dividends, and part from investors coming to believe the Skyrizi and Rinvoq transition would work. Holding on still took patience. The shares closed at $197.99 on April 29, 2026, then reached about $291.48 this morning.

Optimism depends on Skyrizi and Rinvoq growing in the mid-20% range and Apogee working out. The worry is that Humira and Imbruvica fall faster than the new drugs can make up for. Imbruvica already dropped 29.4% last quarter.

On valuation, the trailing P/E of about 120 looks extreme because one-time acquisition charges have pushed reported earnings down. The forward P/E of about 18 tells a calmer story. My main concern is that the shares are trading above the average analyst target of $283.19, along with the question of where growth comes from after 2028. AbbVie also has negative shareholders’ equity, meaning its liabilities exceed its assets on the books, leaving little room for a deal misstep.
Income investors with a 10-year horizon may find AbbVie’s record worth exploring further. A dividend that has tripled since 2016 makes it easier to ride out the next pullback.

title: Google drags down Wall Street stocks
summary: Wall Street's main stock indices flashed red Thursday as investors dropped shares in the parent company of Google following results that fanned concerns over whether the global technology boom can be sustained.Wall Street's main stock indices were lower in midday trading, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropping 1.3 percent.
paragraphs: Wall Street's main stock indices flashed red Thursday as investors dropped shares in the parent company of Google following results that fanned concerns over whether the global technology boom can be sustained.
After a mostly downbeat showing across Asia, Europe advanced, with the European Central Bank leaving interest rates unchanged after the Federal Reserve maintained US borrowing costs on Wednesday.
The euro dipped after Christine Lagarde announced she would step down as the ECB's president in February, but then rose as she signalled a likely rate hike in December.
Crude prices shed more than one percent on reports of renewed diplomatic efforts between the United States and Iran to avoid further strikes.
Wall Street's main stock indices were lower in midday trading, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropping 1.3 percent.
Shares in Alphabet plunged 12 percent. Google's parent company reported after Wednesday's close of trading lower-than-expected profits while it maintained big spending on artificial intelligence.

"It is a rare day when the three big US indices retreat but the small caps gain in tandem with a broad advance in Europe," said market analyst Chris Beauchamp at online trading and investing platform IG.

He noted tech fears had spread to encompass Caterpillar, the construction equipment manufacturer that is the second biggest stock on the Dow index, which faces higher costs to finance its heavy debt load as booming AI infrastructure spending drives up borrowing rates.
Underwhelming results from South Korea's Samsung Electronics also added to doubts about the returns on AI spending.
Samsung, the world's largest maker of memory chips, delivered record quarterly profits but missed market expectations in its semiconductor division.
South Korea's Kospi shares index closed down 1.2 percent, while Hong Kong and Shanghai also fell. Tokyo finished higher.
In other tech news, Microsoft posted forecast-topping revenue and profit, fuelled by its Azure cloud computing division. Its shares initially rose but then fell into the red.
"Tech earnings will remain in focus today with Amazon and Intel reporting" after the US close, said Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid.
Markets had enjoyed a healthy run-up in the previous two days as traders welcomed strong reports from South Korean chip titan SK hynix and an impressive IPO filing from Claude-creator Anthropic.

There was little major reaction to the Federal Reserve's widely expected decision to hold interest rates, as it cited the need for more data in the fight against inflation, which has held stubbornly above officials' two-percent target for five years.

Wall Street's main stock indices flashed red Thursday as investors dropped shares in the parent company of Google following results that fanned concerns over whether the global technology boom can be sustained.

After a mostly downbeat showing across Asia, Europe advanced, with the European Central Bank leaving interest rates unchanged after the Federal Reserve maintained US borrowing costs on Wednesday.

The euro dipped after Christine Lagarde announced she would step down as the ECB's president in February, but then rose as she signalled a likely rate hike in December.

Crude prices shed more than one percent on reports of renewed diplomatic efforts between the United States and Iran to avoid further strikes.

Wall Street's main stock indices were lower in midday trading, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropping 1.3 percent.

Shares in Alphabet plunged 12 percent. Google's parent company reported after Wednesday's close of trading lower-than-expected profits while it maintained big spending on artificial intelligence.

"It is a rare day when the three big US indices retreat but the small caps gain in tandem with a broad advance in Europe," said market analyst Chris Beauchamp at online trading and investing platform IG.

He noted tech fears had spread to encompass Caterpillar, the construction equipment manufacturer that is the second biggest stock on the Dow index, which faces higher costs to finance its heavy debt load as booming AI infrastructure spending drives up borrowing rates.

title: Elon Musk is a 'real genius', Putin says after satellite talks with SpaceX boss
summary: The Russian President praised Musk and said they are in "close" contact.
paragraphs: Elon Musk is a 'real genius', Putin says after satellite talks with SpaceX boss
Elon Musk is a "real genius", Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Wednesday after revealing the two are in "close" contact about satellite technology.

The remarks came during the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, during which Putin discussed Russia's own satellite internet project Rassvet, which provides internet connections to people from satellites.
"He's a genius, a real genius," Putin said of Musk, according to a translation of his remarks by the BBC. "We are in close contact with our American partners, including Mr. Musk."
Starlink is part of Musk's company SpaceX. The company did not respond to a request for comment.
Putin added that it was important for Russia to be in contact with Musk so Rassvet and Starlink satellites do not "interfere with each other in orbit".
"We and our American partners value this mutually, and despite all the political questions, we are working hard," he said.

Starlink has launched roughly 13,000 of its satellites, according to the company. By contrast there are only a couple of dozen Rassvet satellites currently in orbit, according to online satellite trackers.
The Russian Embassy in South Africa said on Wednesday Rassvet is "Russia's Starlink alternative" and "marks only the country's first steps in this field".
"Russia maintains close contacts with the US on space, including with Elon Musk," the embassy wrote.
Putin's comments about Rassvet and Starlink were made as the US and Russia appear to be growing closer, even as it approaches five years since Putin's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Ukraine relied on Starlink internet in its efforts to keep Russia's forces at bay. But its military last week suddenly suffered Starlink connectivity problems, something Musk has admitted SpaceX did intentionally.
US President Donald Trump earlier this month said he'd struck a deal with Russia to import diesel in an effort to lower gas prices that have skyrocketed due to the US war with Iran.
Then Trump waived certain sanctions against Russia that were set to take effect.
Not long after, a US citizen was released from Russian custody, with US envoy Steve Witkoff referring to Putin as a "humanitarian".

Musk was born in South Africa and then immigrated to Canada before settling in the US. All of his business ventures, including Tesla, SpaceX and Starlink, are based in America, with most operating out of California and Texas.
The billionaire, and off and on again trillionaire, has been one of the biggest political allies and financiers of Trump and other Republican US politicians.

title: Sleeping Dogs Movie Director Explains Why The Adaptation Is Taking So Long
summary: Like many video game movies, Sleeping Dogs seems stuck in development hell. summary: I often feel compelled to beeline my way through games--I'll do plenty of optional quests, but rarely do I find myself slowing down to take in the sights or just goof around.
